full_judgment: 21. In support of the said contentions, Mr. Murad Reza, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. Mohammad Shahidul Islam and Mr. Md. Golam Hasnaen, the learned Advocates for the petitioners of writ petition Nos.7409 of 2023 and 11432 of 2022 submits that the nature of land shall be determined as per the latest record of right and until the next survey is done, the nature cannot be changed, for, to that effect Gazette notification is required to be published. In this regard, he submits that vide section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, (in short, the Act of 1950) mutation khatian is the latest record of right and for the preparation of mutation khatian, no gazette notification is required. Apart from that, he submits, section 4 of the Act, 2017 stipulates the provision for changing the nature of land which was recorded in the relevant khatian under another nature. Moreover, even after joint survey is carried out the Deputy Commissioner can still change the nature of land under section 4(4) of the Act of 2017. In the instant case, he submits that the respondents did not follow the said procedures. In addition to that the petitioners in their respective writ petitions have categorically asserted that the lands in question are commercial in nature with supportive documents includirfg mutation khatian (Annexure:B-E2 respectively). Said assertions have not been specifically denied by the respondents concerned. In the given context, finalising the award of compensation treating the properties in question as "Vitta /Bari" is unlawful and hence, not tenable in the eye of law.
